bundles.name: Gaming
bundles.description: The native Linux gaming stack: launchers, Wine and Proton, performance overlays, controller support, and a full lineup of console emulators. Ryoku installs the matching 32-bit GPU drivers for full hardware capacity.

bundles.name: Audiophile
bundles.description: EasyEffects, patchbays, mixers, and PipeWire inspection for people who care how the machine sounds.

bundles.name: The Influencer
bundles.description: A complete stream, record, edit, reformat, caption, and publish kit: recorders, editors, audio and thumbnail tools, plus a right-click video toolkit in the file manager.

bundles.name: Office Worker
bundles.description: FOSS office suites, PDF reading and editing, mail and calendar, Teams, and a Windows app fallback.

bundles.name: SecPulse Basic
bundles.description: Nmap, Gobuster, OpenVPN, wordlists, and the HTB and TryHackMe starter kit, without pretending to be Kali.

bundles.name: SecPulse Advanced
bundles.description: Nikto, Shodan, the ProjectDiscovery recon suite, masscan, firewall helpers, and proxied ops tooling.

bundles.name: The Ricer
bundles.description: Aether and the must-have apps for shaping the desktop, inspecting colors, and editing visuals.

bundles.name: The Vibecoder
bundles.description: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, aider, and the terminal helpers for building with AI.

bundles.name: The Developer
bundles.description: Zed, the Docker stack, git and database TUIs, and the per-project glue for actual development.

bundles.name: The Hacker
bundles.description: Disassemblers, debuggers, memory and disk forensics, hex and binary inspection, and packet work.

bundles.name: CachyOS Kernel
bundles.description: Swap in the performance-tuned CachyOS kernel. Pros: snappier desktop and gaming. Cons: adds the CachyOS repo, DKMS rebuilds, more bleeding-edge. Stock kernel stays as the fallback.
bundles.tagline: faster kernel · keeps stock as fallback
